evidence: Shared queue contracts are owned by website-product-data.
Shared contracts are classified as significant changes.
Significant changes require an approved written plan before implementation.
approvalOrBlocker: A written plan must define scope, non-goals, dependency order, safety boundaries, rollback or recovery, and focused validation.
nextAction: Request or approve the written plan, then update Data before consumers.

evidence: Clearing shared Azure state requires fresh user approval.
Agents must not reset shared state without approval.
Queue operations are durable pipeline infrastructure.
approvalOrBlocker: Fresh explicit approval to clear the specified shared queue or state is required.
nextAction: Do not run the clearing action; provide the exact target and impact for approval.

evidence: Bounded read-only repository discovery may use a targeted subagent.

Subagent findings are evidence and must be validated against current code.
approvalOrBlocker: No approval is required for read-only discovery; scope must remain narrow and concrete.
nextAction: Use a low-cost targeted read-only search to locate the relevant focused tests and validate findings locally.

evidence: Git status must be inspected before editing.
Existing uncommitted changes across multiple repositories can obscure the intended release.
The guidance recommends Project QA Commit when unrelated dirty work materially complicates separation.
approvalOrBlocker: Mixed or unrelated uncommitted work requires a QA review or clean separation before widening implementation.
nextAction: Summarize worktree status and recommend Project QA Commit; preserve all existing changes.

evidence: Registry data is owned by website-product-data.

nextAction: Document the proposed registry contract and route implementation planning to website-product-data.

evidence: Non-trivial repeatable operations must search project and repository script indexes first.

approvalOrBlocker: Catalog an existing safe procedure or define a dry-run-capable script; fresh approval is required before destructive execution.
nextAction: Search the script catalog for an existing operation and document target, dry run, recovery, and approval boundary.
